items.q: Why was a 28% cheaper agent run not a win?
items.a: The agent **still never called the tool** being tested, so the metric **didn't answer the decision**.

items.q: What happened when only the harness changed in a model comparison?
items.a: The **winning model flipped**, a **30+ point swing**.

items.q: How is a public benchmark different from an evaluation?
items.a: A benchmark is a **reference set for a short list**; an evaluation is **measurement to make a decision** about your product.

items.q: What should an agent eval actually test?
items.a: The **closest configuration to your real environment**: model plus harness plus tools on your tasks.

items.q: How should you pick eval tasks?
items.a: Cover your real **workload families** (e.g., code understanding vs bug fixing), not one task type.

items.q: Why run each configuration several times?
items.a: Agents are **non-deterministic**, so single runs hide **run-to-run variance**.

items.q: How do you debug an agent that ignores a tool?
items.a: Walk the pipeline: was it available, was it called, what did it return, and did the **final outcome** change? **Stop at the first break**.

items.q: Why did Jarmak optimise for F1 instead of recall?
items.a: Search pulled **295 files when 6 were needed**: perfect recall, **terrible precision**.

items.q: Why isn't an agent flagging a problem enough?
items.a: A **flag is not a gate**: the stop must be **enforced in code**, then escalated.

items.q: What can a 1% false-alarm rate cost?
items.a: At scale, **10,000 human reviews**; budget for **reviewer capacity**.

items.q: Why keep an independent record of agent activity?
items.a: Seeded security issues **passed agent-side checks** but an **independent traffic record** caught them all.

items.q: What's the final source of truth for an agent eval?
items.a: **Production**: measure after deploy, using **shadow mode** when the blast radius is high.
